content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "The quoted dichotomy is verbatim and is used essentially: Lemma 1 invokes \"b = g(z) \\in \\{0,c\\} (because V \\subseteq \\{0,c\\})\", and \u00a77 concludes from S_0 = \u2205 that g \u2261 c. But \u00a73 only proves that V contains at most one POSITIVE number; nothing there or anywhere else in the text excludes negative values of g. The only remark on sign is \"g(x) > -x\", which does not give g \u2265 0. So the step from \"at most one positive value\" to \"V \u2286 {0,c}\" does not follow. The objector's repair is also correct: if g(x) = d < 0, then (4) gives g(x+nd) = d by induction, and each x+nd = f(x+(n-1)d) > 0, contradicting x+nd \u2192 -\u221e. Since this fact is needed but never proved, the necessity/structural obligation is incomplete as written."}
